title: Watertown NY is Seeing a Renaissance in Learning
author: Holly Korbey
summary: Watertown, New York, a working-class community of 30,000 near the Canadian border, is undergoing an educational transformation by implementing evidence-based reading practices while aligning instruction, feedback, and assessment with cognitive science. The shift represents a move from balanced literacy to the science of reading and learning. Educators like third-grade teacher Heather Mulford, who felt defeated by year after year of students making little academic progress, are finding renewed purpose and seeing tangible results. The district's leaders recognize that the science of reading and the science of learning are connected and are working to align all educators in the same direction.
points: Watertown is implementing evidence-based practices in reading while aligning instruction with cognitive science, recognizing that the science of reading and the science of learning are fundamentally connected.

Teachers like Heather Mulford experienced deep frustration when using traditional approaches, watching kids who got it prosper and those who didn't fall further behind, feeling powerless to make a difference.
The district is taking on a significant implementation challenge by shifting from balanced literacy approaches to science-based reading and learning frameworks across all grades.

Educators and leaders in Watertown show profound respect for new evidence-based knowledge and have a palpable, sometimes emotional desire for change that reflects their commitment to student outcomes.
This renaissance represents a working-class community's courageous investment in better instructional practices based on research, not tradition.
quotes: Heather Mulford had been teaching third grade for almost a decade in Watertown, New York, when she began feeling frustrated and defeated. She loved her students in the working-class town near the Canadian border, and was working tirelessly for them.
Year after year, they made little academic progress. The kids who got it, got it, and the kids who didn't, just didn't, and I didn't feel like I was making a difference.
If they came to me behind, they were going to leave behind or further behind.
This district is implementing evidence-based practices in reading while also aligning instruction, feedback and assessment with cognitive science on how humans learn.

Leaders see that the science of reading and the science of learning are connected, and want to get every educator moving in the same direction.” Archived from Bell Ringer (Holly Korbey) on April 20, 2026 by Tim.
